name: Ticket factory — one scoped ticket to a blind implementer, mechanically gated
description: The software-factory floor (authored 2026-08-03, auth: Kevin, present, overnight autonomy — 'grok would work on the implementation of a genesis ticket, simple scoped, he never sees the big picture'). FOUR NODES: (1) snapshot the tree's pre-existing dirt so a peer's edits can never be attributed to this run — this is a shared live tree with 200+ dirty paths at rest; (2) an implementer agent receives ONE ticket carrying its whole world and no vision; (3) the gate verifies scope + yardstick-immutability FIRST and only then runs the ticket's acceptance command, so a run that moved the target fails before its work is scored; (4) notify. SAFETY IS MECHANICAL, NOT INSTRUCTIONAL: the implementer is told not to edit the yardstick AND cannot pass the gate if it does. The notify message reports ok/exit rather than declaring success, because core:exec treats a nonzero exit as a RESULT (ok:false) and this edge fires either way — a success marker here would be unearned. Params: slug (run id, used for the snapshot file), ticket (the whole prompt), allow (comma-separated in-scope paths), protect (comma-separated files the implementer may not touch), gateCmd (acceptance command, run from repo root, only if the gate passes), implementerModel, notify.

meta.description: Attribution baseline. Without it the gate would blame the implementer for the colony's ambient dirt.
The blind implementer: gets fs.read+fs.write+shell because an implementer who cannot RUN its own yardstick is flying blind, and nothing more.
Scope+tamper BEFORE acceptance: a run that edited the yardstick must fail before its work is ever scored.
